findings.title: Payload and phase-load valids still silently deadlock
findings.evidence: With only row 0 loaded, the independent bench held payload row 1, phase_load_valid, and an early descriptor valid for four cycles. The wrapper selected payload, but R1 suppressed payload_ready because phase_load_valid was forwarded; phase_load_ready stayed low because 459 rows were absent. All ready/accept/busy/protocol_error outputs remained zero.
findings.impact: The exact R1 payload-versus-descriptor trigger is fixed, but the three-channel request interface can still wedge silently at a natural final-row/early-commit boundary.
findings.minimal_fix: Arbitrate phase_load_valid too. Before commit, give payload transfer priority over an early phase request and forward phase_valid only when no payload is pending, or implement an explicit LOAD/COMMIT/EXECUTE FSM.

findings.title: Fixed priority has no starvation bound
findings.evidence: In a committed phase, one pending payload was denied while eight repeated descriptors were accepted across active, last-beat overlap, and output retirement. It moved only after descriptor_valid dropped and the pipeline drained. The Boolean arbitration permits this denial indefinitely.
findings.impact: A continuous winning stream can prevent the next phase from ever loading; the contract correctly excludes starvation freedom, so this is an implementation-completeness gap rather than a claim violation.
findings.minimal_fix: Track the frozen 128 descriptor accepts per phase and transition to LOAD, or implement bounded round-robin/age priority with a stated maximum wait.

findings.title: R2 evidence is only one zero signed8 vector
findings.evidence: The sealed test covers one descriptor, three reads, one zero output, and one contention in each phase state. It does not replay the 1728/221184 actual-record workload, all widths, escape, full FIFO, or random output backpressure through the wrapper.
findings.impact: The unchanged R1 datapath is plausible, but wrapper integration has not inherited R1's full actual-record evidence by execution.
findings.minimal_fix: Run the exact M86 actual-record TB through R2 and add randomized payload/descriptor/phase contention without changing the frozen data oracle.

findings.title: Selected invalid loader traffic can abort an in-flight descriptor into fail-stop busy
findings.evidence: A loaded OOB payload was masked while a descriptor won. After descriptor_valid dropped, the OOB request was forwarded during the accepted descriptor's busy window; protocol_error asserted after its first issue, no complete output was produced, and busy remained asserted until reset.
findings.impact: Fail-closed behavior is preferable to corruption, but kill/flush/reset semantics and outstanding-response accounting are not specified at the wrapper contract.
findings.minimal_fix: Add an explicit FAULT state that stops new grants, drains or invalidates outstanding work deterministically, exposes reset-required status, and proves response/tag conservation across the kill boundary.

findings.title: Production contention SVA is not error-qualified
findings.evidence: The unloaded property requires payload_ready for any OOB payload contention, and the loaded property requires descriptor_ready even after poisoned metadata. Both are expected to be false in fail-closed error states; the independent error bench therefore could not instantiate these properties without intentional assertion failures.
findings.impact: Negative verification can confuse correct fail-closed behavior with arbitration failure.
findings.minimal_fix: Gate progress properties with !protocol_error && !metadata_error and add separate assertions for sticky error propagation and blocked accepts.

findings.title: Phase-load is outside selection and observability
findings.evidence: payload_selected and descriptor_selected are onehot, but phase_load_valid is passed directly to R1 and has no selected/grant output. The contract phrase 'only one request channel' is therefore broader than the implemented two-way selector unless explicitly scoped.
findings.impact: Three-channel contention and phase transition debugging is incomplete.
findings.minimal_fix: Expose phase_selected/phase_accept and assert onehot0 across all three request accepts.

findings.title: The exact-SHA runner is not self-identified by the sealed manifest
findings.evidence: The runner pins all design/test/contract inputs, but its own SHA is absent from input_sha256.txt and RUN_COMPLETE.txt. The independent review freezes the observed runner SHA as fb93c22e...e6b.
findings.impact: The design evidence is reproducible, but the receipt alone cannot authenticate which runner revision enforced the checks.
findings.minimal_fix: Record the runner SHA and tool version in the sealed receipt before launch.

scoped_go: GO for closure of the exact M86-R1 payload-versus-descriptor simultaneous-valid trigger in both committed and uncommitted states.
GO for preserving onehot payload/descriptor selection and exclusive acceptance on the directed R2 wrapper milestone.
no_go: NO-GO for calling R2 a complete three-channel or starvation-free arbiter.
NO-GO for actual-record integration, module-cycle speedup, M78/M88 readmission, system speedup, SRAM/PPA, energy, accuracy, DATE, or best-paper claims.

required_next_gate: Replace the two-input Boolean selector with a LOAD/COMMIT/EXECUTE/FAULT phase FSM that arbitrates phase_load_valid.
Bound execution to the frozen 128 descriptors or provide a formal fairness limit.
Qualify progress SVA in error states and specify deterministic kill/reset behavior.
Replay all 1728 phases and 221184 descriptors through the repaired wrapper before any broader admission.
